Subject: Separation schematic & evidence for Emerald Health SIG request

Hi Claire / Emerald security team,

Thanks for your SIG request. Attached is an initial schematic (separation-schematic-v1.pdf) that summarizes the network and tenancy isolation model we run for Dedicated and Private deployments. High-level notes:

- Control-plane split: management/control-plane services run in a logically isolated VPC reserved for operator-only access; control-plane endpoints accept management connections only over mTLS and customer traffic is never accepted on those interfaces.
- Data-plane rings: inference hosts (dedicated GPU pools) are in separate data-plane subnets per-customer with strict egress and inter-subnet ACLs; shared services (metrics, proxy) are in separate read-only telemetry lanes.
- Key management: customers in Private deployments may integrate their KMS; for Dedicated we offer a tenant-scoped key wrap model.
- Audit evidence: we have packet-flow logs, per-route ACLs, and a minimal set of diagrams mapping SIG/CIS controls to resources — listed in the follow-up bundle.

Can you confirm whether you want editable diagrams (Visio/Draw.io) or a single PDF export? Also please confirm the deadline for the SIG/CAIQ response — we can produce the annotated evidence bundle within 3 business days once scoping is final.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa, thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifications before we start mapping controls:

2) KMS: please describe key rotation responsibilities and which keys are customer-managed vs Redwood-managed. We also need the HSM/KMS vendor name where applicable.

4) SOC 2 mapping: can you include a short mapping to SOC 2 CC controls for the separation design (e.g., CC6.1 logical access, CC7 change management)?

Also, please include a short paragraph describing how we handle model snapshot egress / model artifact export for Dedicated customers — Emerald is especially sensitive to unencrypted model snapshots leaving their network.

Claire — thanks, answered inline (and attaching v2).

> 1) tenancy boundaries for Dedicated vs Private
- Dedicated: tenancy is enforced at the network and hypervisor level. Each Dedicated customer gets a tenant VLAN/subnet and exclusive GPU hosts when requested; hypervisor-level scheduling is constrained to that tenant's hosts. Shared services (e.g., central logging aggregator, build pipeline) are in distinct VPCs with tightly scoped peering and no inbound access from tenant subnets.
- Private (VPC-on-customer): control plane runs in a private operator VPC with a customer-managed peering/VPN. Customer controls the ingress to data-plane; Redwood components that operate inside customer VPC are deployed as tenant-scoped instances with file-system encryption and an enforced node identity (mutual TLS + instance certificate).

> 2) KMS + rotation responsibilities
- Private: customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / GCP KMS) — customer controls root key and rotation; Redwood requests only wrapped keys for runtime operations.
- Dedicated: tenant-scoped key wrap service backed by Redwood-managed HSM (Thales Luna or cloud-native HSM depending on region). Rotation is automated on a 90-day cadence; customers may opt for BYOK for Dedicated with an SLA/onboarding addendum.

> 3) Evidence formats
- Attached: separation-schematic-v2.pdf (annotated), plus a Drive folder with the editable draw.io source and a CSV mapping SIG->artifact (link below). Will provide CSV mapping in final bundle.

> 4) SOC 2 mapping
- We will include a short SOC 2 mapping table in the evidence bundle. Preliminary mapping: CC6.1 (logical access) -> per-tenant ACLs, per-route allowlists; CC7 (change management) -> build/release audit trail + canary rollouts via Redwood Console; CC3 (system operations) -> telemetry agents and tamper-evident logging.

> model snapshots egress
- Default: model artifact exports are disabled by default for Dedicated tenants. When enabled (customer opt-in) exports are only possible to pre-approved storage endpoints and are encrypted in transit and at rest. For Private deployments, export remains subject to customer policy. We capture export approvals in an audit record tied to customer identity.

Scheduling: Tue 21 Sep 14:00-14:30 UTC works for me; Jonas will cover the network diagram walkthrough, Karthik will cover SOC/SIG mapping.

Thanks,
